title: a durable Action's success descriptor orders its fields by UTF-16 code unit, not by UTF-8 byte
notes:
Pins the ONE order a durable Action's success descriptor may be recorded in, at the exact boundary where the two backends can silently disagree. Field order is not cosmetic here: the descriptor's field list is hashed into the successSchema digest and, through it, into the Action contractDigest, so two orders are two different contracts for one accepted program. The three printed lines are the field names in descriptor order, the successSchema digest, and the contractDigest — the names make the divergence legible and the two digests make the case fail even if a future change stops exposing the descriptor.

Measured, not assumed. Before compiler/forkbridge/durable.go.txt was corrected on 2026-08-28 this exact program produced, from the two backends over the same source with neither reporting a diagnostic: reference fields [m, 😀a, �b] successSchema e7483e5c… contract 80f2824f…; Go fork fields [m, �b, 😀a] successSchema 30e7866f… contract 3b2f51d3…. Re-measured by reverting the corrected sort under this exact case, which scored js pass / go FAIL with all three lines differing, then restoring it. The fork sorted descriptor properties with Go's native `<`, which is UTF-8 byte order; the reference sorts with `compareText` (poc/src/durable/schema.ts:128, applied at :401), which is UTF-16 code-unit order. The two orders differ exactly when names straddle the surrogate range, because an astral character is a surrogate pair beginning at 0xD800 in UTF-16 but four bytes beginning at 0xF0 in UTF-8, while U+E000–U+FFFD are three bytes beginning at 0xEE–0xEF. `m` is in the case as a control: ASCII sorts first under either rule, so a case that only ever printed `m` first would prove nothing.

Why the corpus was blind to this: every other 17-durable case names its fields in ASCII, where the two orders coincide, so a live cross-backend digest divergence scored `0 divergent`. That is the green-scoreboard-over-a-real-divergence failure conformance/README.md warns about, and this case exists to close it. It was proved load-bearing rather than assumed: swapping the two expected field names in this file's `stdout` made it fail on BOTH backends with the diff printed, and the file was then restored byte-identically.

Deliberately NOT pinned: `Flow.plan.digest`. The two backends already mint different Plan digests for the same program — measured here with an all-ASCII control, which diverges identically — so pinning it would make this case red for a reason that has nothing to do with field order. 17-durable/static-plan-shape-is-digest-pinned pins the Plan's shape and its digest WIDTH for the same reason. SOURCE NARROWED 2026-08-28, expectation unchanged. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` became enforced (compatibility.mdx §Mandatory, previously unimplemented), and this program read an index without narrowing, so it was correctly refused. §Mandatory's own guidance is that such a read 'MUST be narrowed, or read through an extraction helper'. The narrowing is inert at run time — the guard never fires — so the stdout this case pins is byte-for-byte what it was, re-derived by running both backends. ACCESSOR MOVED 2026-09-01, expectation unchanged. This case read the Action descriptor off `Flow.plan.actions[0]`; it now reads it off `Flow.manifest.actions[0]`. `MIGRATION-PLAN.md` step 12 makes the Effect Manifest the artifact every reporter reads, and this case's observation could not move at step 11 because the Manifest's action row carried only `{id, version, contractDigest}` while the observation is about the SCHEMAS. Step 12 widens the row to carry `inputSchema`, `successSchema` and `errorSchema`, and the widening costs the Manifest digest no discriminating power: `contractDigest` is already `digest({id, version, inputSchema, successSchema, errorSchema})` (poc/src/durable/schema.ts, re-derived and refused on mismatch by `validateActionContractDescriptor`), so two Flows whose Actions differ in any schema already differed in this row. The declared stdout is byte-for-byte what it was and was re-measured on BOTH backends through the new accessor; what moved is where the descriptor is read from, not what it says. That is also why THIS case is the one that proves the widening is not a re-transcription: its two digests are the successSchema digest and the contractDigest, and a Manifest row that re-derived the schemas instead of carrying the descriptor's own would have to agree on both to stay green.
